summary: This note covers the history and records of the Super Bowl Most Valuable Player award, which has been given every year since the first Super Bowl in 1967. It notes which players have won the award most often, the 1971 exception where a player from the losing team was honored, and the 1977 co-MVP selection. It also describes the award's presenters over time and the most recent winner, Nick Foles of the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl LII.
one_line: A summary of the Super Bowl MVP award's winners, records, presenters, and the Pete Rozelle Trophy, through Super Bowl LII in 2018.
key_facts: Tom Brady is the only player to have won four Super Bowl MVP awards.
Joe Montana has won three Super Bowl MVP awards.
Bart Starr, Terry Bradshaw, and Eli Manning have each won the Super Bowl MVP award twice.
Starr and Bradshaw are the only players to have won the Super Bowl MVP award in back-to-back years.
Chuck Howley won the 1971 Super Bowl MVP award as a Dallas Cowboys linebacker despite the Cowboys losing Super Bowl V to the Baltimore Colts.
Harvey Martin and Randy White were named co-MVPs of Super Bowl XII, the only time co-MVPs have been chosen.
Seven Dallas Cowboys players have won Super Bowl MVP awards, the most of any NFL team, including the Super Bowl XII co-MVPs.
Quarterbacks have won the Super Bowl MVP award 29 times in 52 games.
The Super Bowl MVP award has been given annually since the first Super Bowl in 1967.
Through 1989 the award was presented by SPORT magazine; since 1990 it has been presented by the NFL.
Bart Starr was the MVP of the first two Super Bowls.
At Super Bowl XXV the NFL first awarded the Pete Rozelle Trophy, named after former NFL commissioner Pete Rozelle, to the Super Bowl MVP.
Ottis Anderson was the first winner of the Pete Rozelle Trophy.
Nick Foles of the Philadelphia Eagles was the MVP of Super Bowl LII, held on February 4, 2018.
In Super Bowl LII Nick Foles passed for 373 yards and three touchdowns and scored a fourth touchdown as a receiver, becoming the first player to both throw and catch a touchdown pass in a Super Bowl.
